Benchmarking Agents in Insurance Underwriting Environments

paper.arxiv.2602.00456

Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

Substantive bounded primary methods/results/limitations source review is documented at 2602.00456v1. Rule-defined synthetic underwriting evaluation and judge calibration establish construction/protocol scope. Table/prose correctness discrepancy remains; no real-insurer deployment or compliance inferred. Original author/source-verifier/adversarial receipts bind every exact approved fact; unread pages, unreplicated experiments and source conflicts remain recorded in the pinned dossier. This admission is for one logical paper work only.

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The correctness judge is calibrated against one expert’s annotations on held-out 100-trace samples, and hallucination detection conservatively targets nonexistent insurance products; neither metric covers all business-domain reasoning failures.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

UNDERWRITE co-designs fictional insurance rules, data and tasks with Chartered Property Casualty Underwriters; a separate GPT-4.1 user simulator interacts with the agent, and outcome correctness, tool exceptions and uncertain user replies are distinct evaluation criteria.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Six seed task types and 3, 000 GPT-4.1-generated fictional applicant profiles inform task creation; experts revise and accept tasks, and the reported evaluation uses 300 accepted tasks with up to 50 user-interaction turns.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Table 1 reports Claude Sonnet 4.5 answer correctness of 90.30%, with 0.520 tool exceptions and 0.28 uncertain user replies on average per trace; correctness and interaction-error measures have different units.
